title: Cleverbridge says a third party copied payment card data stored on its platform
date_note: Cleverbridge's incident page says it detected unauthorised activity on 4 November 2026 and began notifying affected individuals on 20 November; the event is dated by the start of notification, the disclosure. BleepingComputer reported it on 22 November.
geo_basis: the sources read give no location for Cleverbridge or the affected customers
summary: E-commerce and payments provider Cleverbridge says it detected unauthorised activity on its platform on 4 November and that a third party copied stored payment card data. A notification letter seen by BleepingComputer lists card number, expiry date and CVV/CVC, and says no other personal data such as names, contact or billing details was copied. Cleverbridge says it was not ransomware. Notifications began 20 November; no count given.
plain: A company that handles online payments for software sellers says someone copied stored payment card details, including card numbers and security codes, and it is writing to affected customers.
exec: Cleverbridge says a third party copied stored payment card data; BleepingComputer's notification letter lists the CVV/CVC among the fields.
action: Cleverbridge advises affected customers to check their card statements carefully and tell their card issuer right away about any transaction they do not recognise.
impact: Payment card data of an undisclosed number of customers, per Cleverbridge and its notification letter.

validation.note: Primary: Cleverbridge's own incident page (undated) states the 4 November detection, the copied card data and the 20 November notifications. BleepingComputer quotes the notification letter for the card fields; aitnews relays BleepingComputer and the Cleverbridge page. Cleverbridge did not answer BleepingComputer's questions on the number affected or how attackers got in. ZATAZ (23 Nov) independently reports the copied card data and adds that Cleverbridge rules out ransomware.

review.note: unsourced description: dropped Software provider label and exec fraud-risk claim; ransomware denial attributed to Cleverbridge not ZATAZ; dates, card fields, advice, no count checked against Cleverbridge page, BleepingComputer, ZATAZ
